implemented: Element::text_area reuses the controlled TextFieldState/TextEdit, ScrollSpec and clipboard contracts; canonical text, selection, scroll and byte policy remain client-owned.
One source-indexed grapheme row map drives wrapping, hit testing, selection, caret, visual navigation and bounded visible-row painting.
Pending GPU frames do not defer client updates or fresh CPU input geometry; unrelated wallpaper redraws do not rewrap idle Notes.
Notes fills its actual resized bounds and saves accepted content only through the existing root persistence coordinator.
Single-line, masked and multiline placeholder opacity comes from the shared design recipe and semantic token.

cpu_measurement.contention: Existing video-wallpaper VM remained running; no isolated-host claim.
cpu_measurement.timing_scope: Optimized host CPU-only UI layout/edit/navigation at an 8192-byte client bound; one CPU quota; existing video VM remains running. No GPU/native delivery or end-to-end latency claim.

native_acceptance.scope: Real compositor focus, Enter/Shift navigation, external clipboard, thumb dragging, restart persistence and exact settings/wallpaper restoration.

limits: One optimized host run with a one-CPU quota and a running video VM. These observations are not timing thresholds, a statistically repeatable result or a before/after CPU improvement.
Layout/edit/navigation timings cover CPU view/layout/input synchronization and current-model updates/reveal; they exclude GPU, native input delivery, count/geometry assertions and scene teardown.
Visible-row painting is bounded, but layout still measures the full client-owned document. This is an 8192-byte Notes editor, not virtualized large-document layout.
No current desktop RSS, GPU completion, scanout, end-to-end input latency or native 60 FPS result is established by this measurement.
Complex-script shaping, bidirectional layout, font fallback, preedit/IME and native interoperability remain separate requirements. Accessibility remains deferred by the user.
There is no stationary-pointer selection autoscroll timer. Selection reveal remains input-driven.
